extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, judges, and law students
extracted.subtask_description: Index/excerpt from a patent law treatise summarizing legal doctrines, standards, and evidentiary rules governing patent validity, infringement, assignments, remedies, reissues, and related procedural topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel to deny validity of assigned patent
rubrics_metrics.description: estoppel of assignee to deny validity of assigned patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes/citations: estoppel of 1021; though patent actually void 787 n.1; though assignee might have known the patent void 787 n.1; procuring a valid patent after assigning the invalid for value enures to benefit of assignee 787; joint-patentee assigning and then obtaining sole patent holds it for benefit of assignee 787 n.3. (Usage: limits an assignor/assignee from contesting validity in certain circumstances.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and remedies of assignee against assignor
rubrics_metrics.description: rights of assignee against assignor; contract relations of assignee governed by usual law of contracts; breach of assignment may also be an infringement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rights to recover purchase-money (1229-1231); obliged to refund if assignor creates a legal title destructive to prior equitable title of assignee 1229 n.3; remedy when assignee refuses to accept transfer 1234; rights of assignee against third parties 1227–1232.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignor remedies and defenses
rubrics_metrics.description: remedies of assignor for breach of conditions in the assignment; when assignee procured the assignment by fraud
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refs: recovery of purchase money 1287–1248; fraud in procurement of assignment 1236; assignment consequences and related remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association standing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An association must sue in equity in the names of its members
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index note: association must sue in equity in the names of its members 1101. (Implication for standing and form of equitable actions.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumpsit and waiver of tort in infringement cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumpsit for infringement — the tort being waived
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited entries: assumpsit for infringement, the tort being waived 989, 111, 1091, 1098. (Procedural note about pleading/waiver.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and duties of patent attorneys (power of attorney etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Who may be patent attorneys; relation to Patent Office; power of attorney (form); revocation; effect of assignment; ratification by assignee; confined to attached application; duties and limits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: power of Commissioner over attorneys 431; appointed by special power of attorney 439; power of attorney, form 432; revocation 433; how affected by assignment 488, 789; ratification by assignee 438; authority confined to the application to which power is attached 434; principal bound 435; duties (not to delay to prejudice principal 578); disclaim without consent of principal 689 n.6; cancel claims and abandon application 579 n.2; acts bind foreign principal 689 n.6; compensation and lien 436; how disbarred 437; and guidance to see related topics (Application for Patent, Disclaimers, Power of Attorney).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bankruptcy court has no power over letters-patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Bankruptcy court, no power over letters-patent; proceedings do not affect letters-patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index notes: bankruptcy proceedings do not affect letters-patent 766; that plaintiff in bankruptcy is no ground of abatement 956; see also Assignments, Insolvency, Judicial Sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bond and account as alternative to injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: When bond and account ordered in lieu of an injunction; amount of bond
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry: bond and account when ordered in lieu of an injunction 1202; amount of bond 1202. (Guidance for equitable remedy alternatives.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of parties' books and records in accounting/profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Books of plaintiff/defendant when produced on accounting and inspection of defendant's books as to profits
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: books of plaintiff as evidence on accounting 1157; defendant's books inspection as to profits 1143; when books are evidence 1127. (Evidentiary guidance for equitable accounting.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof — general rule in patent cases at law
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden of proof in patent cases at law — how satisfied and allocation of burdens between parties
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General index entry referencing many sub-issues (inventive skill, prior use, publication, utility, abandonment, first inventor, specification fraud, description ambiguity, excessive claims, surrendered/repealed patent, infringement voluntariness, foreign patent limits, estoppel, disclaimer timeliness, infringement, co-ownership/license status, damages, profits, title by assignee). See many specific sub-entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof as to inventive skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden of proof as to inventive skill — how satisfied
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed reference: burden as to inventive skill, how satisfied 1022; degree of inventive skill indicated by removal of serious defects 113 n.2; inventive skill in combinations 155 a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof as to prior use
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden of proof as to prior use — how satisfied; requisites of notice of prior use
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refs: burden as to prior use 1026; requisites of notice of prior use (Allis v. Buckstaff) 1004 a.5; prior use must communicate the invention to the public (Cahill v. Brown) 330 n.; secret use not prior use (many citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof as to publication (prior publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof that prior publication anticipates or affects patent validity — how publication must communicate invention to public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: publication 1028; prior publication must communicate the invention to the public 330 n.; priority of publication vs priority of invention discussed in cases (Booth v. Lyman, Cox v. Griggs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof as to utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of utility — utility is actual, not comparative
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: utility 1029; case Cook v. Ernest (1872) notes utility is actual, not comparative 342 n.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof as to abandonment to the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof that invention was abandoned to the public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abandonment entries 1030; effect of abandonment to the public discussed in many cases 346 n.; abandonment may result from acts of inventor at any time 351 a.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden regarding the true inventor and priority
rubrics_metrics.description: On defendant to show patentee not a true inventor (and issues re first inventor)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: on defendant to show patentee not a true inventor 1023; the first inventor 1024; priority of conception/reduction to practice discussed (Farmer v. Brush, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden as to specification fraud, ambiguity, excessive claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof that specification is fraudulent, description ambiguous, or claims excessive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: specification fraudulent 1034; description ambiguous 1036; claims excessive 1036; effect of failure to claim clearly described matter 890 n.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden as to patent surrendered/repealed or term limited by foreign patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof that patent has been surrendered or repealed; term of patent limited by foreign patent
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent surrendered or repealed 1038, 1039; term of patent is limited by foreign patent 1043; Canadian patent takes effect when 623 f.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee or grantee must prove title
rubrics_metrics.description: On assignee or grantee to prove title to the patent rights
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index: on assignee or grantee to prove title 1040. (Evidentiary allocation in suit.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases and doctrine: use of precedent
rubrics_metrics.description: In citing patent cases, the facts must be considered — doctrine of cases criticized/discussed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index note: cases, in citing, the facts must be considered 1177 n.4; doctrine of cases criticized and discussed with many examples. (Guidance on reliance on precedent.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of principles, ideas, and their reduction to practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Principle (idea) as such not patentable; principle reduced to practice may be patentable; patent covers all modes of reducing to practice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several case references: principle not patentable (e.g., Darcy v. Allin, Househill v. Neilson); principle reduced to practice is patentable (American Bell Telephone Co. v. Dolbear); patent covers all modes of reducing to practice 130 n.1, 141 n. See also entries on 'principle' defined and test cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability distinctions: art, process, manufacture, and machine
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and distinctions among 'art,' 'process,' 'manufacture,' and 'machine' and their patentability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexed entries: 'art/process/manufacture/machine' defined and discussed (e.g., Cochrane v. Deener, Detmold v. Reeves); differences affect patentability (art/process may be patentable subject-matter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Double use and analogous use doctrines
rubrics_metrics.description: Double use (same product used for lawful and unlawful purposes) and analogous use concept in anticipation/novelty analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple citations on 'double use' (e.g., Bean v. Smallwood, Bray v. Hartshorn); analogous use discussed 259.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination patents: co-operation of elements and sub-combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles governing combination patents — co-operation of elements, whether making a part constitutes infringement, sub-combinations, combination equivalents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: co-operation of elements in combination 155 n.1; combination-patent may be infringed by making an element to be united by others 924 n.1; combination-patent not infringed by use of a part 928; re-issue of combination patent may cover sub-combinations (Gill v. Wells, Christian v. Ramsey); measures to distinguish old and new in claims 525 n.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-issue rules and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: When re-issue is allowable and how it may alter claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-issue allowable only where error arose from inadvertence, accident, or mistake (Conklin, Coon v. Wilson); re-issue may enlarge claims 656; re-issue confined to matter attempted to be described/claimed in original 663; decision of Commissioner on re-issue as to fraud is final 715 n.1; courts' duty to sustain honest and correct re-issue 684.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to practice and diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduction to practice—necessity, proof by prior inventor, measurement of reasonable diligence in reducing to practice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: reduction to practice necessary 125; mechanical perfection not necessary 129 n.; measure of reasonable diligence 887, 387; reduction to practice by prior inventor as proof 891 a.1; conception vs reduction to practice and connecting diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public use vs experimental use and secret use
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinction between public use (bars patent) and experimental/secret use (does not)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: public use defined as use without restrictions (Egbert v. Lippman 356 a.1); experimental use not public 855 a.3, 318; secret use not prior use (Dollond's Case, etc.); experimental use producing profit still may be experimental (Elizabeth Pavement Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior publication and priority of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior publication must communicate invention to public to defeat novelty; priority of publication vs priority of invention
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: prior publication must communicate invention 330 n.; priority of publication is prima facie proof of priority of invention (Booth v. Lyman); circulation and proof issues discussed in multiple cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive skill: standards and indicia
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree and nature of inventive skill required for patentability; indicia such as removal of serious defects, novelty of combination, instantaneous inventive act
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: nature of inventive skill 78 n.; inventive act may be instantaneous 83; inventive skill indicated by removal of serious defects 113 n.2; inventive skill in combinations 155 a.; degree required discussed in Clark Patent S. & F. R. Co. v. Copeland.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction and rules of interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Court to construe patent and jury to apply it; liberal vs strict construction; parol evidence to aid construction; effect of omitting application oath
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: court to construe, jury to apply 732 a.1; patent liberally construed 736 n.1; strict construction of letters-patent referenced 16a; parol evidence to aid construction 732 a.; effect of omitting application oath 458.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of equivalents and its tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaning and scope of 'equivalent' in infringement analysis — equivalence resides in use, tests for equivalent, equivalents performing additional functions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: 'equivalent' defined 248; equivalence resides in use not in nature 249; equivalents may perform additional functions (Goodyear); equivalents in improvements 257; tests and examples cited (American Pin Co. v. Oakville Co.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies: injunctions, damages, and accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: Available remedies in patent litigation: preliminary and permanent injunctions, damages, equitable accountings, profits, and their measures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: purpose of preliminary injunction 1171 n.; injunction after patent expires against use of infringing articles 1211 n.; measures of damages and profits (profits presumed, measure of actual damages 1068; profits are what defendant made in excess of what he could have made by using another invention 1062); interest on damages 1066; increase of damages by court 1069 n.; account incident to discovery or injunction 1091.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses: implied licenses, scope, transferability, and licensee rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on implied licenses of purchasers and licensees, scope and transferability of licenses, and rights/duties of licensees
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: implied license to vendee from recovery of royalties 830 n.1; implied license of purchaser in open market 824 n.; licensee must sue in name of legal owner 938 n.1; licensee repudiating license liable as infringer 819 n.5; patentees may restrict license use territorially 824 a.; license transferable or not as parties choose 823 a.; licensor enjoined from declaring license revoked 124 n.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct remedies at law vs in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctions between remedies at law and in equity (e.g., injunctions vs damages) and consequences for pleading and procedure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: remedies at law vs equity distinguished 1050; account ordered in equity though no injunction needed 1091 n.1; actions in equity vs at law referenced throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder of inventions and claim multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about joinder of inventions in one patent/claiming multiple species vs generic claims; claims not to be unnecessarily multiplied
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: joinder of inventions and appropriate practices 469, 470 a.; joinder of generic and specific claims barred or regulated (Bwart, Ex parte); claims not to be unnecessarily multiplied 521 ft.; joinder of art and apparatus 478.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of expert testimony and role of jury
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert witnesses may assist court; jury decides anticipation under court direction using expert evidence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: expert evidence may aid court in construing patent 1014 a.4; jury to decide whether one patent anticipates another under court direction and on expert evidence 1014 n.4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy and nature of patent privilege
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent privilege as a conditional grant to inventors (not a contract); policy of protecting inventors and disclosure purpose
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: patent privilege a conditional grant not a contract 15 a.2; policy of protecting inventors 33 n.; nature of patent privilege discussed widely (benefits conferred, statutory basis, territorial limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests for identity of machines and articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests and difficulty in determining identity of machines/artifacts for infringement/anticipation purposes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: identity of machines and its test 178 n.1; identity a difficult question (Butterworth v. Hoe); tests and examples cited across cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of sale, exhaustion, and territorial limits on monopoly
rubrics_metrics.description: Lawful sale of patented article takes it out of monopoly; territorial and importer rules; effect of vendee's rights
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: lawful sale takes article out of monopoly 824 a.2; patentees' territorial limits 46 s.; patentees cannot restrict vendee's rights by subsequent legislation 828 n.8; vendee may use until used up 826 a.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abandonment by describing and not claiming
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandonment can occur by describing prior matter and not claiming it; effect on re-issue and later patents
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: abandonment by describing and not claiming 352 a.; effect of failure to claim clearly described matter 890 n.5; abandonment may result from acts of inventor at any time 351 a.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means vs ends and patentable subject-matter limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention is a means, not an end; function or result is not patentable per se
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries: invention is means not end 90 n.1; function/result not patentable 147 n.1; many cases reiterate 'means not end' principle.
